Rishi — draft below (quick pass). I'm keeping the tone concessional but specific so procurement has clear acceptance criteria. Please flag any policy items.

PROPOSED SEC EXHIBIT LANGUAGE (redline-ready):
1) Bounded Inspection. Customer may schedule an inspection of Redwood's operational controls limited to the specific systems and artifacts listed in Appendix A (Evidence Matrix). Redwood will provide a 30-day notice period for on-site or remote inspections. Inspections shall be limited to sampling bands not to exceed 10% of production subsystems in any 12-month period. Unless otherwise agreed, inspections must be completed within a 7-day window.

2) Penetration Testing. Customer may engage a mutually-agreed third-party assessor to perform penetration testing against Redwood's staging environment. Prior to testing, Customer must provide: (a) a scope document, (b) a signed NDA covering testers, and (c) at least 7 business days' notice. Staging access will be ephemeral and limited to test accounts; production credentials will not be provided. Any critical findings must be disclosed to Redwood within 72 hours and Redwood will have 30 days to remediate or propose a mitigation plan.

3) Evidence Cadence & Rampdown. Redwood will deliver: (a) quarterly evidence bundles mapped to SOC 2 assertions (CSV manifest + secure links), and (b) an annual SOC 2 package when available. Archived artifacts will remain accessible for 60 days after archive date; after that Redwood may apply an evidence rampdown and provide summaries in lieu of full artifacts.

Notes: 
- The "sampling bands" approach is intentional to limit operational load.
- We should avoid language that permits "unfettered access" or unbounded forensic inspections.

I can convert this to tracked changes in MSA art.7 and prepare a short appendix template (Appendix A = Evidence Matrix reference). Recommend we attach redline_MSA_v2.docx with these edits.
